column1: # 1.21.1 -> 26.3 renames, applied by scripts/port/gen.py to the generated source tree.
# Cumulative: the 26.1 and 26.2 blocks are kept verbatim, because a rename that landed in 1.21.9 or 26.1 still
# applies here and there is no mapping file to diff against any more (26.x is unobfuscated, so every
# row comes from a compile error). New 26.3 rows go in the last section.
# Format: `old<TAB>new`. Whole-word replacement, string literals included.
# The 26.1 rows are cumulative on top of the 1.21.11 ones: 26.1 is the first unobfuscated release,
# so there is no Yarn mapping to diff against any more and every row has to come from a compile
# error. Keeping the 1.21.11 block below means a rename that landed in 1.21.9 still applies.
# Rows with a package path come first (the generator sorts longest-first).
# Derived from the Loom mappings of both versions, joined on the intermediary name, and filtered to
# the names this source tree actually uses. Regenerate the candidate list with scripts/port/candidates.py if a
# future error looks like a rename that is missing here.
# 26.3 renamed the flag a second time (1.21.1 `hasImpulse` -> 1.21.9 `hurtMarked` -> 26.3
# `syncVelocity`), and this table is applied in one pass ordered by pattern length, so the inherited
# `hasImpulse -> hurtMarked` row would win and leave the intermediate name behind. The row is
# rewritten here instead of added to: the intermediate name is unreachable in a single pass.
# The GUI render layer was renamed to the "extract" model: a screen no longer draws, it extracts a
# render state, and the whole drawing surface moved to GuiGraphicsExtractor with shorter names.
# The two phrase rows are what makes that a table entry instead of a 33-file edit; they must be
# longer than the bare type row below, which the generator's longest-first ordering guarantees.
# Every row here is qualified by its receiver or by the call that produced it: the bare names are
# generic enough that a future caller could mean something else entirely.
# The declared version ranges have to be rewritten too: `~1.21.1` means "below 1.22", which 26.1
# falls outside, so both loaders refuse to load the mod before any class runs. Each pattern is
# anchored on word characters at both ends, which is what the generator's whole-word match needs.
# 26.2 moved the whole screen stack onto Gui: Minecraft no longer has a `screen` field or a
# setScreen method, Gui does. That pair is not a table row, because the Fabric package
# `net.fabricmc.fabric.api.client.screen.v1` contains the same `client.screen` text: it lives in
# PvScreens instead. The chat and the overlay message moved one level further, onto the Hud that
# Gui now owns, and the "hide the HUD" flag became Hud.isHidden(). Rows that would end in a closing
# parenthesis drop it, because the generator's whole-word match needs a word character at both ends
# 26.2 deleted MultiBufferSource and RenderBuffers: geometry goes through the submit queue, which
# PvWorldGeometry wraps. Only the two camera/target accessors that moved are left here.
# The sixteen separate *_WOOL items became one ColorCollection, indexed by DyeColor.
# Three pure renames. The two that also changed arity are in PvCompat instead, because a table row
# ---- 26.3: GLFW is gone, the window layer is SDL ----
# 26.3 dropped lwjgl-glfw for lwjgl-sdl, so `org.lwjgl.glfw.GLFW` is not on the classpath at all.
# The key constants moved to `com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.InputConstants`, and they are SDL *scancodes*
# now: `KEY_W` is 26, not GLFW's 87. That is also what a KeyMapping default holds in 26.3 (vanilla's
# `key.forward` is constructed with 26), and what `KeyEvent.key()` returns, so every comparison in the
# screens keeps its shape and only the constant changes. Names that differ from the GLFW spelling:
# ENTER -> RETURN, KP_ENTER -> NUMPADENTER, CAPS_LOCK -> CAPSLOCK, LEFT_/RIGHT_ modifiers lose the
# underscore (LSHIFT / RCONTROL / LALT), and SUPER -> GUI.
# The two fields of a key event swapped roles with the window layer: `key()` is the scancode now and
# `keycode()` the layout code, so the screens keep comparing `key()` and pass `keycode()` along.
# The input type enum lost the KEYSYM/SCANCODE split: one keyboard type covers both.
# PoseStack lost the quaternion overload of mulPose; the same rotation is now `rotate`. The Matrix4f
# overload stayed, which is why this row is anchored on the argument instead of the method name.
